### [0983181](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0983181c821ca683790aa486f2c881644d733f63)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T15:29:54Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): sm_103a NVFP4 context programs release the scale slot early and deepen the packed K/V ring (#9177)

Cake's NVFP4 paged-context attention takes E4M3 (FP8) queries and
outputs and NVFP4 K/V pages with E4M3 block scales. The kernel
dequantizes the pages to E4M3 in shared memory. It uses head dim 128,
bottom-right causal masking and HND pages. The family ships 22 AOT
programs. On each of sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300), it ships two
fixed-size programs and nine runtime-size programs. The fixed-size
programs cover one shape class: 32 query heads over 4 KV heads, with
host-scalar or device-scalar scales. The runtime-size programs,
`RUNTIME_PACK<p>_SM100A` and `RUNTIME_PACK<p>_SM103A`, cover GQA packs
1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 16.

Today on sm_103a, the softmax stage waits in each KV block before it
reuses its scale slot. It waits until the correction (rescale) warps
have rescaled the output and dequantized the next K/V tile. The ring of
packed NVFP4 K/V tiles also has only two stages. As a result, the loads
run at most one block ahead of the dequantization.

This PR changes the 11 sm_103a programs: the two fixed-size programs and
the nine runtime-size programs. The correction warps now release a
stage's scale slot as soon as they read the scale. The packed K/V ring
now holds 8 tiles, which uses 160256 B of dynamic shared memory per CTA.
Each ring barrier is initialised by its own lane, so short one-tile
launches do not pay for the deeper ring. Routing does not change. The 11
sm_100a programs keep their schedule, names and bytes. The arithmetic
does not change. In every timed row and layout, O is bitwise equal to
the previous program and to the JIT module.

On GB300, across 28 rows, this PR is 1.009x to 1.263x faster than the
previous Cake program. It is 1.457x to 3.812x faster than the JIT
module. Each row is faster than both the previous program and the JIT
module in each of the 10 memory layouts. No row is slower. The largest
gains are on long-KV rows with few query tokens: 1.263x on 2 x 1 x 4096
and 1.222x on 1 x 32 x 32768. The smallest gains are on one-tile
launches: 1.010x on 1 x 1 x 16 and 1.009x on 1 x 16 x 64. This PR is
faster than trtllm-gen on 22 rows, by 1.004x to 5.158x. trtllm-gen is
faster on six rows, where trtllm-gen/PR is 0.842 to 0.982:

- 1 x 32 x 32768: 0.842
- 2 x 1 x 4096: 0.881
- 1 x 16 x 64: 0.924
- 1 x 1 x 16: 0.973
- 1 x 4096 x 16384: 0.981
- 16 x 256 x 2048: 0.982

### [02b8714](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/02b8714ab405f8def56d0cb90ad873a7f93569ea)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T15:19:20Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp): faster backward and checkpointed step on the non-deterministic KDA KCP route (#9155)

Cake ships KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training as four packages:
deterministic and non-deterministic, each available single-rank and with
context parallelism over packed documents (KCP). This PR speeds up
`cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp`, the non-deterministic KCP package. This PR
is faster than the same package on main on 107 of 108 rows by more than
the A/A band (run-to-run noise measured by timing two identical copies,
defined below). One row, GB300 shape B fwd (1.008x, band 1.8%), is
within noise. No row is slower.

Each cell is the range over that GPU's 36 rows of baseline time / this
PR's time (this PR's 3-run median for `main`, its run-1 time for the
other baselines); above 1.000x means this PR is faster. All GPUs: CUDA
13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

- Shapes: Shapes F and G use an uneven 5-document pack of 250,750 tokens
on 16 ranks. Shapes A and B scale that pack down 4x on 4 ranks (each
document about a quarter as long, rounded up; 62,689 tokens). Shapes H
and I scale the C-E pack up 4x on 16 ranks. No row measures the raw gate
without the q/k L2 norm.
- Ops: `fwd` is a forward that saves for backward, `bwd` is the backward
alone, and `fwd+bwd` is both. `ckpt` is an activation-checkpointed step:
a forward that keeps only the cross-rank states
(`checkpoint_keep="states"`), then a recompute forward, then the
backward. Every arm uses head dim 128. The Cake arms use the
per-document zigzag layout, `workspace=None` and the package defaults.
- `main` is this package at the PR's merge base 983ca7d6 (unchanged on
main since). `main` and `this PR` are medians over 3 runs. Each run also
times a second, identical copy of `main` and of `this PR`. `A/A band` is
the largest relative difference between a copy and its twin over the
row's 3 runs. A row counts as faster only when `main / PR` - 1 is larger
than the band.
- `det, pre-#9141` is the deterministic Cake KCP package before #9141,
and `det, #9141` is the same package with #9141 (now on main). `FLA
0.6.0` is flash-linear-attention 0.6.0 with context parallelism (the
faster of its contiguous and zigzag configs per row). It is the
same-precision non-Cake baseline: the only non-Cake KDA training
implementation with context parallelism at this package's precision in
this comparison. `cuDNN KDA (ref.)` is the cuDNN frontend KDA built from
tag v1.32.2 (whose `__version__` string reads 1.33.0) on the cuDNN
9.24.0 backend, best config per row. It keeps more of its FP32
intermediates in BF16 than this package and its gradients are less
accurate against an FP64 reference, so it is shown for reference only.
It is faster than this PR on these rows:
- GB200 (16 rows): fwd on A-D and F-I; bwd and fwd+bwd on C, D, H and I.
- GB300 (14 rows): fwd on A-D, F, G and I; bwd on C, D, H and I; fwd+bwd
on D, H and I. C fwd+bwd ties at 1.000x.
  - R200 (4 rows): fwd on A-D.
- Timing: each sample is the slowest rank's CUPTI GPU span of the call,
from the beginning of the first kernel to the end of the last kernel. A
run reports the median of 48 samples from 3 groups. Each group visits
the arms in order and then in reverse order, with 8 samples per arm each
way. A 258 MiB L2 flush precedes every sample. Execution is eager (no
CUDA graphs), and the arms of a run are interleaved in one process on
the same GPUs. Run 1 times all arms; runs 2 and 3 time only `main`,
`this PR` and their identical copies.
- The baselines were timed only in run 1, in the same process as this
PR, so their `/ PR` columns divide by `this PR (run 1)`. This PR's run-1
times differ from its 3-run median by up to 7%, and 12 rows differ by
more than 2%. The baseline ratios come from one run and carry that
run-to-run variation. Against `det, #9141`, three rows are within the
A/A band of their row: GB300 F bwd (1.039x, band 4.5%), R200 F bwd
(1.015x, band 1.9%) and R200 G bwd (1.057x, band 6.4%). Each baseline
ratio compares arms timed in the same run (run 1). `main / PR` divides
the two 3-run medians, and both arms are timed in every run.

The other three Cake KDA training packages, `cake_kda_det_train`,
`cake_kda_nondet_train` and `cake_kda_det_train_kcp`, support the same
gate and q/k L2-norm modes, and all four ship for sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [1112164](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/11121641b9eea7bfceda1afc20f784a036e4bb2c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T14:49:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fp8_rowwise_gemm_allreduce): grid lockstep throttle for large SM90 calls (#9164)

`flashinfer.comm.fp8_rowwise_gemm_allreduce` with `backend="cake"` runs
a row-wise scaled FP8 (e4m3) GEMM and the all-reduce over 2, 4 or 8
ranks on one node, in one fused kernel per call, and returns a BF16
output on every rank. It supports one data type combination: FP8 e4m3
inputs with per-row and per-column scales, and BF16 output. It ships on
sm_100a (#8379), sm_103a (#8605) and sm_90a (#8905, with the per-call
six-reducer layout from #9101). This PR changes sm_90a only. It adds two
generated sm_90a programs with a grid lockstep throttle, one on the
four-reducer layout and one on the six-reducer layout from #9101, and
selects them per call. In a throttled program, the producer of each CTA
begins a tile only when no CTA is more than two persistent rounds ahead
of the grid's count of begun tiles. The wait is bounded and traps after
the same cycle budget as the cross-rank waits. A call runs a throttled
program when its raster group is larger than one and it has at least
12288 output tiles. An 8-rank call with the 4096-row capacity does not
use the throttle. The throttled programs compute the same result, and
every other call runs the existing program. Of the 144 measured cases,
24 select a throttled program: 10 mlp and 3 o_proj cases at 2 ranks, 8
mlp cases at 4 ranks and 3 mlp cases at 8 ranks. The other 120 run the
same program as before.

## 2 ranks

Setup: one node of 8 NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (sm_90a), CUDA 13.0, driver
535.216.03, torch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7. Every row shows absolute
times for:

- previous: the previous Cake version, which is FlashInfer main
including #9101.
- this PR.
- torch: `torch._scaled_mm` row-wise FP8 GEMM (cuBLASLt, BF16 output)
followed by `torch.distributed.all_reduce` in BF16 (NCCL). This is the
strongest applicable non-Cake baseline. It is the standard PyTorch path
for the same GEMM and gives the same BF16 all-reduce result on every
rank.

Each time is the CUPTI GPU time of one call. Each session runs 200 ms of
warm-up, then 1000 ms timed. We take the median per rank, then the
slowest rank. Each process loads one FlashInfer version and also times
the torch baseline. Processes run in the alternating order previous,
this PR, this PR, previous. "previous / this PR" compares the two
versions through the torch baseline timed in each process. A value > 1
means this PR is faster. "torch / this PR" is torch time divided by this
PR time. A value > 1 means this PR is faster. The "throttled program"
column shows yes or no.

A row is FASTER when previous / this PR > 1.02 and SLOWER when it is <
0.98. Otherwise it is PARITY. A row is INCONCLUSIVE when it fails a
check:

- the two sessions of an arm differ by more than 2 %, or
- a session's dispersion exceeds 0.05, or
- the SM clock floor (0.95 x 1725 MHz) is not met or cannot be resolved.

INCONCLUSIVE rows show measured times but no ratio and no direction.

### [de9e7c5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/de9e7c5bda520ed9cbb24213247248575de9e96d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T14:41:04Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_lm_head_det_train): keep the default step's peak within the logits-materializing bound (#9152)

`flashinfer.cake_lm_head_det_train` is the deterministic chunked LM-head
training backend. It takes BF16 inputs, accumulates in FP32, and
produces outputs and gradients that are bitwise reproducible from run to
run. It has two entries:

- The loss entry, `cake_lm_head_det_train_loss`, with CE and policy
objectives.
- The log-probability entry, `cake_lm_head_det_train_logprob`, with an
optional scalar or per-token temperature.

The fast form follows #5680. It keeps one chunk of logits plus an FP32
`[V, H]` weight-gradient accumulator. On some shapes, such as those in
#7545, its step peak is higher than an implementation that keeps the
BF16 logits of the valid rows would need, which is `B = 2*T_v*V + 2*V*H
+ 2*T*H` bytes:

- T is the number of rows.
- T_v is the number of valid rows, meaning rows whose label is not -100.
- H is the hidden size.
- V is the vocabulary size.

Before this PR the fast form was the default. `memory_mode="budget"` was
an opt-in form that limits the step peak by recomputing part or all of
the weight gradient in the backward, one vocabulary block at a time.
This PR changes the default to `memory_mode=None`. This automatic form
chooses between the fast and budget forms for each call, based on the
predicted step peak against B. It works as follows:

- It applies to a call that forms a BF16 weight gradient on CUDA,
meaning W requires a gradient and grad mode is on.
- It keeps the fast form as long as the fast form's predicted step peak,
with its own buffer lifetimes, stays within B minus a 2 % margin.
- Otherwise it runs the budget form the planner picks, if one fits. If
none fits, it keeps the fast form.
- A call whose valid rows fit in one 4096-row chunk always keeps the
fast form. Its step peak can be higher than B: the one-chunk rows below
measure up to 1.12 B.
- It plans on the valid-row count from the forward, or on the caller's
`num_valid_rows`. An uncompacted call (`compact_rows=False`) without
`num_valid_rows` keeps the fast form.
- `memory_mode="fast"` keeps the previous default form.
`memory_mode="budget"` forces the budget form, as before.

**Measurement.** All numbers are a same-GPU A/B of FlashInfer main
(c8a4d8a2) against this PR merged onto that main. Timings were taken at
this PR's commit f8c27a5a. Later commits change only tests, the
benchmark script, documentation, typing and two host-side details of the
budget backward (listed below), with no kernel, launch or plan changes.

- For each (row, temperature) pair, two units run on two different GPUs.
Each unit runs main, the PR and a second copy of the PR in forward
order, then in reverse order, with one process per tree.
- Times are CUPTI kernel times with the L2 cache flushed: 4 rounds x 4
iterations per process (16 rounds per tree), taking the median per tree.
- Speedup is main / PR. Its 95 % CI comes from a hierarchical bootstrap
with 4000 resamples. The A/A band is max(1 %, the CI bound of PR-copy /
PR).
- GPUs: B200 (sm_100a, driver 580.82.07, 1000 W), GB300 (sm_103a, driver
580.159.03, 1400 W) and R200 (sm_107a, driver 620.43, 2300 W).
- Software: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0 runtime) in a CUDA 13.4
development container, using prebuilt kernels with no JIT.
- Shapes: BF16 inputs and chunk 4096. H / V is 6144 / 154880 unless the
row says otherwise (other rows use 4096 / 154880 and 5120 / 248320). 5 %
of labels are ignored, except 33 % on the two #7545 rows. Temperatures
(none, scalar 0.7, per-token) apply only to the log-probability entry.

Step (forward + backward) speedup, main / PR, per GPU. Peak / B is the
measured step peak (forward through backward, including outputs and
gradients) divided by B, shown as main → PR; a slash separates values
that differ across the three GPUs. ↓ means slower beyond noise: PR /
main is above 1 + band and its 95 % CI lies entirely above 1. ↑ is the
reverse case (faster).

What the table shows:

- **Two-chunk rows (T = 8117, H 6144):** peak drops from 1.67-1.71 B to
0.98 B. Step is 0.851-0.912, so 10-17 % slower, and every cell is slower
beyond the band.
- **Four-chunk rows (T = 16172 / 16231 / 16384, H 6144):** peak drops
from 1.10-1.12 B to 0.85-0.86 B. Step is 0.979-1.015; 14 of 45 cells are
slower beyond the band, by at most 2.1 %.
- **#7545 rows (T 16384, 33 % ignored, three chunks):**
- H 6144: peak drops from 1.36-1.38 B to 0.98 B, and step is 0.933-0.950
(5-7 % slower).
- H 4096: peak drops from 1.13 B to 0.86-0.87 B, and step is 0.953-0.979
(2-5 % slower).
- **H 5120 / V 248320, T 16384:** main is already at 0.98 B. The PR
picks the budget form on some GPUs (0.75 B) and keeps the fast form on
others. Step is 0.986-1.005.
- **H 4096, T 16384 rows that keep the fast form (0.87-0.89 B):** step
is 0.977-1.002; 7 of 15 cells are slower beyond the band, by at most 2.3
%.
- **One-chunk rows (T 2048, 4097) and rows with eight or more chunks (T
32463 to 65031, already at 0.40-0.69 B):** form and peak are unchanged.
Step is 0.985-1.017, all within the band.

In the other timed operations, the budget rows' forward (fwd) is slower
because the budget form does more work in the forward, and their bwdk
can be much faster. Across all 340 timed cells per GPU (68 rows x 5
operations), faster / parity / slower is:

- B200: 7 / 285 / 48
- GB300: 7 / 250 / 83
- R200: 8 / 284 / 48

Callers who want the previous default form can pass
`memory_mode="fast"`.

<details>
<summary>Other timed operations whose verdict is beyond the A/A band on
at least one GPU</summary>

The operations are:

- fwd: forward with autograd
- fwdng: forward without grad
- bwdk: backward of an untimed forward
- ckpt: non-reentrant checkpointed step (2x forward + backward)

Also in this PR (review follow-ups):

- The loss entry's recompute forms now also save the labels through the
autograd context. An in-place write to the labels between the forward
and the backward therefore raises PyTorch's saved-tensor version error.
This matters because an uncompacted call's recompute reads the caller's
labels tensor.
- The weight-gradient recompute gathers rows from detached views of X
and W. As a result, a backward under `create_graph=True` no longer
rejects its `out=` row gather.
- `benchmarks/bench_cake_lm_head_det_train.py` now reports the step time
with a cache miss (`step_miss_ms`) and the step peak over B. It also
times full steps with a backward that frees the graph, and rejects
`--ignore-frac` values outside [0, 1].

The module ships for sm_100a (B200/GB200), sm_103a (B300/GB300) and
sm_107a (R200).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Cake training now automatically selects a memory strategy for eligible
calls that compute weight gradients. Explicit fast and budget modes
remain available.
* Calls with gradient-enabled weights can use the opt-in training
backend, including when gradient tracking is disabled.
* **Benchmarks**
* Training benchmarks now report step timing and peak-memory
measurements, including comparisons with binding caches cleared.
Deterministic benchmarks allow selecting the memory mode.
* **Documentation**
* Updated guidance explains memory-mode selection, routing, and
binding-cache behavior.

### [645df66](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/645df662fa7191a77a5f42fcfe26eccf489737e6)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T14:35:10Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_moe_grouped_gemm_det_train): address review comments from #9132 (#9173)

Follow-up to #9132. This PR fixes five of the six CodeRabbit review
comments on that PR. The sixth comment says the prebuilt `aot/` loader
does not compare a library's closure. That code is in `cake_build.py`, a
byte-identical template that all Cake packages share, so we will fix it
in the template for all packages.

## Changes

- **`KeyError` in the JIT fallback.** `_jit_cuda_version()` passed the
placeholder name "an accumulate build" to `cake_build._jit_toolchain`.
Sometimes FlashInfer's JIT cannot be imported, as in a prebuilt-only or
vendored copy. In that case the error message called
`prebuilt_path(name)`, and that call raised a `KeyError` that nothing
caught. So `prepare_wgrad(accumulate=True)` raised an error. It should
have fallen back to the composed route (`accumulate_reason ==
"min_cuda"`). The function now passes a real `build.json` library name.
- **Unbuildable accumulate library counted as loadable.**
`_jit_cuda_version()` now returns `None` in three cases:
  - `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT` is set.
- `get_cuda_path()/bin/nvcc` does not exist. FlashInfer's version query
then falls back to `torch.version.cuda`.
  - The CUDA path cannot be resolved (`OSError`).

If an accumulate build is not prebuilt, it now uses the composed route
and shows the existing once-per-process warning. The fused and composed
routes give bit-identical results. The probe reads FlashInfer's
toolchain module from `sys.modules` after `_jit_toolchain` imports it.
This keeps the JIT fallback in `cake_build.py` as the package's only
`flashinfer` import. The standalone import-surface test checks this.
- **Output span check.** The wgrad preparation compared `num_groups *
out.stride(0)` with the 32-bit element limit. This check missed a
one-group `out` with an expert stride of 0, as from `expand` or
`as_strided`. The check was already on main, and it also covers the
overwrite route. The check now bounds the whole addressed span, `1 +
sum((size - 1) * stride)`. It also bounds each stride, because the
binding takes strides as 32-bit values. It raises the existing
`ValueError` before it allocates or binds anything.
- **Stream ordering in the acceptance test.**
`test_five_repeats_under_copy_streams` and `test_changing_offsets_cycle`
create the counters and traffic buffers on the current stream. They now
call `torch.cuda.synchronize(device)` after that and before the gemm and
traffic streams use the buffers.
- **NaN passed the bf16 budget.** The acceptance test now asserts
`torch.isfinite(got).all()` and counts `~(err <= bound)`. A NaN now
counts as out of budget.

## Performance

Only host-side checks change. Kernels, generated programs, build entries
and launch plans do not change, and every shape launches the same
programs and plans as main.

## Tests

- New CPU tests:
- The real `ImportError` path (`sys.modules["flashinfer.jit.core"] =
None`).
- `test_jit_toolkit_needs_nvcc_and_the_jit_enabled`: no nvcc, nvcc
present, JIT disabled, and an unresolvable CUDA path.
- `test_out_span_is_bounded_by_32_bit_addressing`: a one-group `out`
with expert stride 0 and a 2K row pitch, for both overwrite and fused
accumulate. It also covers an expert stride above the limit.
- We ran all 13 `cake_moe_grouped_gemm` det and nondet test files in a
CUDA 13.4 container. The tested files are byte-identical to this PR
head.
- B200 (sm_100a): pre-commit passed (48 files); 1374 passed, 65 skipped,
0 failed.
- VR200 (sm_107a): 0 failed in 12 files; 167 passed in the determinism
file.
- GB300 (sm_103a): 1371 passed, 68 skipped, 0 failed on the previous
revision of this change, which differs only by `strict=True` on one
`zip`. The run at this head is queued.

### [5a3757b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5a3757be9a01621d1f3531f57a216591249fb859)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T14:33:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gqa_nondet_train): run the host-boundary checks on side streams beside bwd_pre (#9165)

`cake_gqa_nondet_train` is Cake's packed-varlen causal GQA training
attention for head dim 256 (BF16 I/O, FP32 accumulation). This PR
follows #9140 and #9149. It changes how the backward schedules its
host-boundary checks. It changes no kernel and no plan.

When the caller passes host sequence boundaries (`cu_seqlens_q_host` /
`cu_seqlens_k_host`), the backward queues two device checks that the
host and device boundaries agree. One is a range check on the tile table
and the other is a key check on `cu_seqlens_k`. On FlashInfer main, one
side stream runs the one-CTA plan kernel and then both checks, which are
a chain of seven small PyTorch kernels. The main kernels wait for that
chain. On GB300 the chain runs slower while it shares the GPU with
`bwd_pre` and finishes after `bwd_pre`, so the main kernels begin late.
This PR splits the work into two shorter chains on two side streams, and
both run while `bwd_pre` runs:

- The first side stream runs the plan kernel, then the range check.
- The second side stream runs the key check, which reads `cu_seqlens_k`
only, then the row-map fold order.

The main kernels wait for both chains. The same checks run, and a
disagreement still fires a device-side assert before the main kernels
write. Without host boundaries nothing changes: one side stream runs the
plan kernel and the row-map fold order, as on main.

All 9 shapes x 3 ops (fwd, bwd, step = 2 x forward + backward) were
measured on GB200 (sm_100a), GB300 (sm_103a) and R200 (sm_107a) against
FlashInfer main in the same mode (both sides with host boundaries, or
both default). Speedup is baseline time / this PR's time, so above 1 is
faster. On GB300 with host boundaries, the `zz_cp8_r3_120000` backward
goes from 11.136 ms to 11.077 ms (1.005x, A/A noise ±0.22 %). Its step
goes from 17.634 ms to 17.525 ms (1.006x, ±0.23 %). These two rows are
faster beyond noise. Every other row is within its A/A noise band in
both modes, and no row is slower beyond noise.

The speedups over the fastest same-precision non-Cake implementation per
row in the same run (FA4 PR2968, FA4 PR3059 gen, cuDNN FE expand or
cuDNN FE expand det) are:

- Backward: host boundaries GB200 1.080x-1.215x, GB300 1.174x-1.280x,
R200 1.105x-1.347x; default GB200 1.064x-1.206x, GB300 1.156x-1.285x,
R200 1.074x-1.350x.
- Step: host boundaries GB200 1.078x-1.156x, GB300 1.121x-1.189x, R200
1.072x-1.276x; default GB200 1.075x-1.138x, GB300 1.110x-1.186x, R200
1.053x-1.279x.

The deterministic Cake package on FlashInfer main is
`cake_gqa_det_train`. Since PR9151 it uses the same side-stream plan and
exact host-boundary chunks. It was timed beside this PR in a second run
per GPU. In both modes this PR is about as fast as it:

- Backward: host boundaries GB200 0.994x-1.009x, GB300 0.997x-1.008x,
R200 0.997x-1.011x; default GB200 0.996x-1.009x, GB300 0.996x-1.001x,
R200 0.997x-1.001x.
- Step: host boundaries GB200 0.986x-1.008x, GB300 1.000x-1.005x, R200
0.989x-1.010x; default GB200 0.993x-1.003x, GB300 0.997x-1.003x, R200
0.992x-1.003x.

Small calls (8 layouts) are not in the tables. With host boundaries, the
small-call backward is faster than main on all three GPUs: GB200
1.044x-1.149x, GB300 1.046x-1.135x and R200 1.024x-1.128x. Without host
boundaries, one small-call row is slower beyond noise: the R200
`empty_and_short_k` step, which goes from 0.109 ms to 0.110 ms (band
±0.53 %). Its backward is within noise. Two forward rows with host
boundaries are also outside their bands: GB200 `tile_edges` (0.987x,
0.015 ms, band ±0.67 %) and GB300 `tails_small` (0.956x, 0.029 ms ->
0.030 ms, band ±2.46 %). This PR does not change the forward, so these
two rows are measurement noise of 15-30 us calls.

### R200 (sm_107a)

NVIDIA R200 (VR200 board) (sm_107a, 212 SMs), CUDA 13.4 (packages built
with nvcc cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130),
driver 620.43. Cold L2 (read flush + delay kernel before every call),
CUPTI kernel span per call, median of 24 samples (8 groups x 3
iterations, arm order rotated per group), eager (no CUDA graphs). BF16
I/O, FP32 accumulation, FP32 LSE, GQA 24 query / 4 KV heads, head dim
256, causal (bottom-right) packed varlen, scale 0.0625; dK/dV are FP32
row-map adds into caller buffers. step = forward + forward replay +
backward (2 fwd + bwd, one call). Speedup = FlashInfer main / this PR
(above 1 is faster), each with and without host boundaries; A/A noise =
FlashInfer main against itself in the same run. Tables 2 and 3: speedup
= baseline / this PR (above 1 is faster). The non-Cake arms ran in the
same run as table 1; the deterministic Cake package of FlashInfer main
(`cake_gqa_det_train`) ran beside this PR in a second run with the same
protocol.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* Host-boundary validation now checks both range capacity and key
coverage, including when tile plans are built through the fallback path.
* Single-range capacity overflows and boundary disagreements are checked
consistently across planning modes.
* Backward processing now waits for boundary checks to complete before
continuing, helping ensure validation results are respected.

### [6eea3d5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6eea3d59838441811ee72c7b7590f98cd823c8fa)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T14:16:19Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train): narrow-output programs and accurate split-K weight gradients (#9171)

`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train` is the nondeterministic Cake
training dense GEMM. It has two kernel families, both accumulating in
FP32:

- K1, the BF16 projection GEMM: forward, input gradient (dgrad) and
weight gradient (wgrad). Output is BF16, or FP32 for the gradients. It
supports transposed and strided views and MLA batched head layouts.
- K2, the FP32 router GEMM: forward, dgrad and wgrad for hidden 4096 /
5120 / 6144 -> 256 experts.

This PR changes the programs and routes of the narrow-output K1 rows
(forward and dgrad with d_out <= 1024, and small wgrads) and of the
router wgrad.

- Forward: a one-wave program for the 512-column rows (sm_100a,
sm_103a).
- Dgrad: an nvjet-style program for thin BF16 rows, and a narrow-output
FP32 program (both sm_100a, sm_103a).
- Forward and dgrad: faster existing programs on measured rows (sm_100a,
sm_103a, sm_107a).
- Wgrad: a stream-K program for 5120 -> 1024 with a fixed reducer per
split tile (B200, and GB300 FP32 at T 16384).
- Wgrad: fixed-order split-K forms for thin FP32 rows, and a two-chain
form for 4096 -> 1024 FP32 on sm_107a.
- Wgrad: the deterministic package's program with a fixed split count
for the router and for the rows where a split form misses the accuracy
bound below.

These forms keep every output within 1.1x of the median error of the
deterministic package at FlashInfer 2e989556, measured against an FP64
reference.

Each table compares the PR with three baselines on the same GPU model:

- main: this package on current FlashInfer main, timed in the same run
as the PR, with its A/A noise band.
- det Cake: the deterministic package `cake_dense_gemm_det_train` on
FlashInfer main.
- SOTA: the fastest non-Cake implementation of the same precision class
(BF16 inputs, FP32 accumulation, same output dtype; for the router,
BF16x9 emulation counts as FP32). Candidates: cuBLAS / cuBLASLt 13.8.0
(heuristic top-24 plus split-K variants), QuACK 0.6.5 (autotuned),
DeepGEMM 2.8.2 bf16_gemm, FlashInfer mm_bf16 backends, CUTLASS stream-K,
and BF16x9 cuBLAS / cuBLASLt for the router. Every SOTA arm whose
determinism was measured repeated bit for bit over 5 runs.

det Cake and SOTA times come from a separate run on the same GPU model.
Timing is CUPTI GPU time with a cold L2, the median of 5 interleaved
groups (10 for rows marked ⁽ʳ⁾), in eager (e) and CUDA graph (g) mode.
Each ratio is baseline time / PR time, so > 1 means the PR is faster.
Software: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.4 toolkit, cuBLAS 13.8.0. "n/a"
means that shape was not measured, e.g. T outside 16172 / 16231 / 16384.

Over the full 328-row representative set, vs main:

| GPU | Arch | Faster | Parity | Slower | Range vs main (graph) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B200 | sm_100a | 67 | 253 | 8 | 0.83-1.20 |
| GB200 | sm_100a | 62 | 262 | 4 | 0.89-1.17 |
| GB300 | sm_103a | 68 | 246 | 14 | 0.86-1.31 |
| R200 | sm_107a | 9 | 304 | 15 | 0.78-1.05 |

Every slower row is an accuracy fix: main's program misses the bound
above there, and the PR's program meets it. The exceptions are a few
R200 rows that run main's program with bit-identical output and differ
only by noise. The tables below list only the rows whose program or
route changed. The full 328-row tables are in the comments.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added optimized dense projection GEMM paths for additional GPU
architectures and workloads, including forward, input-gradient, and
weight-gradient operations.
* Expanded benchmark reports with package-path timings, repeatability
checks, timing classifications, and CUPTI fallback counts.
* **Behavior Changes**
* Certain K2 weight-gradient cases now use the deterministic program
instead of the previous specialized routing.
* PyTorch deterministic-algorithms alerts are documented for selected
non-deterministic launch paths.
* **Documentation**
* Updated routing guidance, benchmark details, accuracy and
repeatability criteria, and tested GPU and software versions.

### [56cb13a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/56cb13af6d6db4b6d283c3f69ab47faa788cd208)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T14:12:24Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): CTA-pair ticket programs wait for the last echo (#9166)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train`, the deterministic DSA (DeepSeek
sparse attention) indexer for training, fuses scoring with exact top-k
selection and returns ids and scores in a fixed order. Of its two
variants, BF16-score (BF16 q/k) and FP8-score (e4m3 q/k with a per-key
FP32 scale), this PR changes only the BF16-score variant. In CTA-pair
ticket scan programs, the first CTA now waits once for the second CTA's
last `st.async` ticket echo before it retires its shared memory. This PR
changes 13 such programs: 4 `pair_l6` programs that sm_100a and sm_103a
share, and 9 sm_107a programs (`pair_l6`, `pair_wide`, `pair_narrow`);
dispatch does not change. This is a correctness fix, not a performance
change; #9147 made the same fix in the non-deterministic package. The
baseline is the deterministic package on current FlashInfer main, and
ids, scores and order stay bitwise identical to it on all 66 rows per
GPU. Speedup (main latency / PR latency; above 1 means the PR is faster)
is 0.985x–1.062x on B200, 0.996x–1.016x on GB300 and 0.990x–1.065x on
R200. No row on any GPU is slower beyond noise, that is, outside max(A/A
band, 1%). The rows that are faster beyond noise (15 on B200, 4 on
GB300, 5 on R200) show small gains.

**B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)**
On the CUDA 13.4 toolkit and torch 2.14.1+cu130, both packages share one
process with CUPTI kernel timing, cold L2 and arm orders (AB, BA,
interleaved). `main ms` and `PR ms` are median one-call latencies;
`speedup` is `main ms` / `PR ms`; `A/A band` is the difference from
timing one package twice. Rows `P1_peaked`, `S4sink` and
`packed11_topic_r01` show the last of 4 rerun rounds (each round: 100
calls per arm and order, fresh process, different GPU).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* Improved coordination at the end of top-k processing when workloads
span multiple processing groups. This helps ensure outstanding work is
fully synchronized before processing completes, across the affected

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [1b2f3db](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1b2f3db710a5a2f8046440236db98b0d468a3b05)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T13:50:52Z
- **提交信息**: cake_gdn_det_train: copy unaligned q/k/v/do to an aligned buffer before launch (#9169)

## 📌 Description

`flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train`
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gdn_det_train`) is the experimental
deterministic single-GPU Gated DeltaNet training package. On main, a
contiguous operand that starts a few bytes past an aligned boundary
makes the launch fail with CUDA error 716 (misaligned address, sticky).
An example is `torch.empty(n + 4,
dtype=torch.bfloat16)[4:].view(shape)`, and `.contiguous()` keeps its
address. Reproduced on B200, this affects `v` and `do` (output gradient)
at 2 B and 8 B past a 16-byte boundary, and `q` and `k` at 2 B. These
operands were already bitwise equal to the aligned operand: `q` at 8 B;
FP32 `g`, `beta`, `initial_state` and final-state gradient at 4 B and 8
B; and BF16 `beta` at 2 B and 8 B.

This PR adds `_aligned(t, align)` in `cake_chain.py`. It returns
`t.contiguous()` and clones it if `t.data_ptr() % align` is nonzero,
before the first launch. An aligned operand is used in place as before.
`PREP_ALIGN_BYTES = 8` applies to `q` and `k` when the TMA prep does not
read them in place, because the plain prep loads 8 bytes at a time.
`ROW_ALIGN_BYTES = 16` applies to `v` when the WY stage does not read it
in place (forward and backward) and to `do` in the backward.

The purpose is correctness, not performance. Aligned operands take the
same launches: 24/24 launch sequences (stage and grid) are identical on
GB300 across 12 shapes x 2 gate regimes. Outputs are bit-identical (48
rows per GPU, 0 differ). The only added host work is about 85 ns per
checked tensor (`_aligned(t, 16)` 165.5 ns vs `t.contiguous()` 80-81 ns
on GB300).

A/B against current main uses 12 representative shapes, four operations
(forward, backward, fwd+bwd and ckpt) and two gate regimes. ckpt is
`torch.utils.checkpoint` with `use_reentrant=False`, which runs 2x
forward + backward. The gate regimes are:
- gL: per-value-head log-decay rates spread from 1e-4 to 1 per token,
times 0.5-1.5 (slow decay).
- gB: `A_h = exp(U[0, ln 16])` per value head and `g = -A_h *
softplus(N(0,1))` per token (fast decay).

Inputs are one packed BF16 `[T, (2H + HV) x 128]` buffer with
`q`/`k`/`v` as head views, FP32 `g`, FP32 `beta = sigmoid(N(0,1))`, BF16
`do`, in-kernel L2 norm, scale 128^-0.5, zero initial state and packed
varlen. Runs use ABBA order (main, PR, PR, main), each in a separate
process, with 8 processes per side per row. Times are medians of the
CUPTI-measured GPU span per call, in ms, with L2 flushed before every
sample. The A/A band is the largest of two values: the gap between two
labels of the same call in one process, and the spread of per-process
medians on each side. On B200, GB300 and R200, all 96 rows (12 shapes x
4 operations x 2 gate regimes) are within the A/A band. No row is slower
or faster beyond it.

Setup: B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07), GB300 (sm_103a, 152
SMs, driver 580.159.03) and R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs, driver 620.43), with
the CUDA 13.4.2 toolkit, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Python 3.13.

The tables show speedup = main / PR (above 1 means this PR is faster),
the A/A band, the GPU busy ratio (GPU busy time PR / main, which removes
host gaps between kernels), the verdict and the processes per side.

<details><summary>B200 (sm_100a): 96 rows, 96 within the A/A band, 0

## 🧪 Tests

- New `test_unaligned_operands_take_an_aligned_copy` has 6 cases (`v` 2
B, `v` 8 B, `q` 2 B, `k` 2 B, `do` 2 B, `do` 8 B). Each runs forward +
backward through `cake_gdn_det`. Every output and gradient (`o`, `dq`,
`dk`, `dv`, `dg`, `dbeta`) is bitwise equal to the aligned operand.
`_aligned` returns an aligned operand itself and copies a shifted one.
- Each GPU ran:
- `tests/experimental/test_cake_gdn_det_train.py`,
`test_cake_gdn_det_train_api.py` and `test_cake_gdn_det_train_names.py`;
- a bits check of 48 rows (12 shapes x view / contiguous x host / device
route), PR vs main and PR repeated 5x;
- the unaligned-operand probe (18 cases, both routes, compared bitwise
with the aligned operand).
- Results:
- B200: 300 passed, 6 skipped; 11 passed; 83 passed. Bits: 0 differ, 5x
all equal. Probe: 18/18 equal.
- GB300: 300 passed, 6 skipped; 11 passed; 83 passed. Bits: 0 differ, 5x
all equal. Probe: 18/18 equal.
- R200: 301 passed, 5 skipped; 11 passed; 83 passed. Bits: 0 differ, 5x
all equal. Probe: 18/18 equal.

Suggested CI targets: `tests/experimental/test_cake_gdn_det_train.py`

### [80c12f4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/80c12f44922bee63c142922835a9289d1f806a50)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T13:18:31Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gated_act_mxfp8): hybrid band path and per-size band-path routing on SM100, SM103 and SM107 (#9138)

`flashinfer.cake_gated_act_mxfp8_det_train` is Cake's deterministic
fused SwiGLU + MXFP8 quantization kernel for training. The forward pass
quantizes `silu(gate) * up` of a BF16 `[M, 2K]` input, and the backward
pass quantizes the gate and up gradients. Each pass writes rowwise,
colwise or both E4M3 outputs, with one E8M0 (RCEIL) scale per 32 values
in the swizzled 128 x 4 layout.

This PR adds a hybrid path for warps whose gate inputs fall in the
sigmoid's saturation band. Warps that fail the fast-path vote compute an
exact branchless sigmoid for every element instead of reloading from
global memory. The PR also routes each size range to the band-path
variant measured fastest. Entries that timed slower than main beyond
noise on unit-normal inputs keep main's program. As a result, the
program changes in 5 of the 30 representative (shape, pass) cells on
sm_100a, 10 on sm_103a and 1 on sm_107a, and every other cell runs
main's program.

Each table compares this PR with the same module on current FlashInfer
main (the previous Cake version) on the same GPU:

- Build: CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92) and PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.
- Timing: CUPTI kernel time, with L2 flushed before every call.
- Runs: main and the PR are interleaved in one process and timed twice
per run over three runs. Each value is the median of the 6 pooled
samples.
- Shapes (M x K, where K is the output width): 128 x 128, 4096 x 2048,
4096 x 7168, 16384 x 7168 and 131072 x 8192.
- Inputs: unit normals, and block-scaled (unit normals times a random
power of two in [2^-8, 2^8] per block).
- Noise band: a result counts as faster or slower only when its speedup
exceeds its noise band. The band is the larger of the A/A offset (two
copies of main's code measured the same way) and main's spread across
samples.

### NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)

None of the 60 results is slower beyond its noise band, and four
block-scaled results are faster beyond it: 128 x 128 fwd colwise
(1.077x), 128 x 128 fwd both (1.057x), 128 x 128 bwd colwise (1.021x)
and 4096 x 2048 fwd colwise (1.059x). Results whose program is unchanged
land between 0.987x and 1.031x, which is run-to-run noise. One of them,
4096 x 2048 fwd rowwise on unit normals at 1.002x, exceeds its 0.17%
band and is marked as noise because its program is unchanged.

### NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs)

Of the 60 results, 13 are faster beyond their noise band. The ten
block-scaled ones are 128 x 128 fwd rowwise (1.095x), fwd colwise
(1.101x), fwd both (1.099x) and bwd colwise (1.072x); 4096 x 2048 bwd
colwise (1.050x) and bwd both (1.053x); 16384 x 7168 bwd rowwise
(1.015x) and bwd both (1.008x); and 131072 x 8192 bwd rowwise (1.015x)
and bwd both (1.005x). The three on unit normals are 16384 x 7168 bwd
both (1.005x), 131072 x 8192 bwd both (1.007x) and 131072 x 8192 bwd
rowwise (1.000x, 1170.29 to 1169.99 µs, beyond a 0.01% band). In this
run one result is slower beyond its band: 4096 x 2048 bwd colwise on
unit normals went from 14.05 to 14.11 µs (0.995x) against a 0.23% band.
A focused re-run of that cell measured it as noise, and the footnote
under the table gives the numbers. Results whose program is unchanged

### [fbf1adc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/fbf1adccaf125c8efbfee2adeb8f311dec8ba626)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T13:18:00Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): split sm_107a FP8 128-head decode at 18-20 rows (#9167)

On FlashInfer main (`18c327b4`), `cake_dsv4` has 36 programs on each of
sm_100a and sm_103a. That is 28 BF16 and FP8 programs for 8 to 128 query
heads and 8 NVFP4 decode programs. sm_107a has 14 FP8 programs:
128-head, 64-head and low-head. This PR adds no program and changes no
program. It changes only the host's split-KV rule for sm_107a FP8
128-head launches with PDL on, when the key width is 1025 to 1152 keys
(nine 128-key tiles).

On main, launches with 1 to 17 query rows split each row's keys into
pieces: 9 per row at 1 to 4 rows, 5 at 5 to 8 rows and 3 at 9 to 17
rows. A merge then combines the pieces. Launches with 18 or more rows
run unsplit as one program. This PR extends the three-piece split to 18
to 20 rows, raising `max_tokens_pdl` from 17 to 20 and the three-piece
cap from 51 to 60 pieces. These launches merge with the existing
three-piece merge program, which the 16- and 17-row launches already
use. Nothing else changes: launches with 1 to 17 rows or 21 or more
rows, 64-head launches, launches without PDL, and sm_100a and sm_103a
launches all run as before.

The baseline is the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main, which runs
18- to 20-row launches unsplit (measured at `d9c9177b`; the `cake_dsv4`
sources and host are identical on `18c327b4`). Against it, calls get
faster by:

- 1.09x to 1.11x at 18 to 20 rows (0.84 to 1.07 us per call) when every
query attends all 1152 keys with 1 query token per request
- 1.09x at 20 rows (0.83 to 0.85 us) with 4 query tokens per request
- 1.13x to 1.15x at 18 and 20 rows (1.24 to 1.32 us) with mixed key
counts

When every query in the call attends few keys, the split adds a merge
launch that the call does not need, and the call gets slower. With all
queries at 128 to 640 keys, calls measure 0.87x to 0.88x (1.09 to 1.13
us slower per call). With all queries at 128 to 384 keys, they measure
0.79x to 0.80x (1.61 to 1.68 us slower). Per-request key counts live on
the GPU and the host does not read them, so it cannot route these calls
differently. The 1- to 17-row split launches on main already behave this
way. The unchanged 17-, 21- and 24-row launches measure 1.00x.

Measured on an NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs) with the CUDA 13.4.92
runtime and driver 615.71.10, using an FP8 KV cache and 128 query heads.
Times are in microseconds per call. Each call is one of 8 back-to-back
calls captured in one CUDA graph with PDL on, and L2 is flushed before
each replay. Each value is the median over 8 rounds (2 processes × 4
rounds). Main and this PR are timed in the same process in alternating
order. Speedup = main latency / this PR's latency.

On a second R200 with 208 SMs, the same rows measured:

- 1.08x to 1.13x with all 1152 keys
- 1.08x with 4 query tokens per request
- 1.14x to 1.18x with mixed key counts
- 0.88x to 0.89x with all 128-640
- 0.80x with all 128-384

On a VR200 (212 SMs, driver 620.43), the same rows measured:

- 1.05x to 1.11x with all 1152 keys
- 1.05x to 1.06x with 4 query tokens per request
- 1.10x to 1.16x with mixed key counts
- 0.86x to 0.89x with all 128-640
- 0.78x to 0.81x with all 128-384

In each of the 8 rounds on all three GPUs, every changed all-1152 and
mixed row was faster, and every all-128-640 and all-128-384 row was
slower.

- **Layer**: "c4 (32K context)" is the DeepSeek-V4 c4 layer at 32K-token
context, with 128 sliding-window keys plus 1024 top-k keys of the
4x-compressed cache per query. "c128 (128K context)" is the c128 layer
at 128K-token context, with 128 sliding-window keys plus 1024 keys of
the 128x-compressed cache.
- **Keys per query**: "all 1152" means every query attends 1152 keys.
"mixed" means every other query attends all 1152 keys and the others
attend 128, 256 or 384 keys. "all 128-640" means every query attends 128
to 640 keys. "all 128-384" means every query attends 128 to 384 keys.
- **Query tokens per request**: 1 (decode) or 4 (multi-token).
- **Query rows T**: query rows in the call.
- **PDL**: programmatic dependent launch, on for every row.
- **Launch (main -> this PR)**: "unsplit -> 3 pieces per row" means main
runs the launch unsplit as one program, while this PR splits each row's
keys into 3 pieces and combines them with the existing three-piece merge
program. Rows marked "(unchanged)" launch the same way on main and this
PR: 3 pieces per row at 17 rows, unsplit at 21 and 24 rows. Their 1.00x
shows the run-to-run variation.

| Layer | Keys per query | Query tokens per request | Query rows T | PDL
| Launch (main -> this PR) | main (us) | this PR (us) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c4 (32K context) | all 1152 | 1 | 17 | on | 3 pieces per row

`cake_dsv4` also has BF16 and FP8 programs for 8 to 128 query heads and

### [9e3d35e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9e3d35ed41b11b259b9ec1db7fbc9ab3380fd064)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T13:02:38Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det_train_kcp): faster backward and checkpointed step on the deterministic KDA KCP route (#9141)

For #6595.

Cake KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training uses BF16 inputs and
outputs, FP32 accumulation and head dim 128. It ships as four packages:
deterministic and non-deterministic, each single-rank and
context-parallel (`flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train`,
`flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train_kcp`, `flashinfer.cake_kda_nondet_train`,
`flashinfer.cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp`). The kernels take either a
precomputed log-decay gate `g` or a raw gate with fused
`A_log`/`dt_bias`, with optional fused in-kernel Q/K L2 norm. This PR
makes backward and the checkpointed step faster in the deterministic
context-parallel (KCP) package, `flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train_kcp`, and
its output bits still repeat run to run. Against the same package on
current main (GPU device time, CP4 on 4 ranks), backward is 1.05-1.06x
faster, forward+backward 1.04x and the checkpointed step (forward +
recompute + backward) 1.09-1.11x. Forward is at parity (0.998-1.004),
and no row is slower than main beyond the noise band. Per architecture,
the device ranges for bwd / fwdbwd / ckpt / fwd and the faster / parity
row counts are:
- GB200: 1.053-1.062 / 1.038-1.045 / 1.097-1.106 / 0.999-1.002, with 65
/ 15 of 80 rows.
- GB300: 1.053-1.062 / 1.038-1.045 / 1.098-1.107 / 0.999-1.002, with 117
/ 27 of 144 rows.
- VR200: 1.050-1.060 / 1.036-1.042 / 1.092-1.101 / 0.998-1.004, with 63
/ 17 of 80 rows.

- Packs (document lengths in tokens, total T, 4 ranks):
  - `ts4` = [24576, 16384, 14336, 10240], T = 65536.
- `c5` = [56843, 59310, 72971, 23218, 38408], T = 250750 (a customer
pack).
  - `c5p` = `c5` plus one 11394-token padding document, T = 262144.
  - `q1` = [28874, 38814, 60180, 121988], T = 249856.
  - `cp8` = [42024, 28768, 36864, 23416], T = 131072.
- Suffix `g` = precomputed gate. Suffix `r` = raw gate. All rows use 64
heads, Q/K L2 norm on, and layout `zigzag_per_document`.
- op: `fwd` = forward. `bwd` = backward. `fwdbwd` = forward+backward.
`ckpt` = checkpointed step (forward, then recompute + backward under
`torch.utils.checkpoint`).
- workspace: `none` = `workspace=None`. `held` = a caller-held
workspace.
- Times: median ms of the slowest rank, 3 groups x 8 samples, arms
interleaved, cold L2. "device" = GPU time. "events" = CUDA-event time,
including host launch.
- A/A: a second copy of main timed against main. A row counts as faster
or slower only beyond max(0.5%, 2*|A/A-1|, the per-group spread).

### GB200 (sm_100a): 80 rows, 65 faster, 0 slower

NVIDIA GB200 (sm_100a), CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, 4 GPUs
of one node.

| pack | op | workspace | main ms | PR ms | speedup | A/A | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The other Cake KDA training variants (deterministic single-rank,
non-deterministic single-rank and non-deterministic KCP) are outside the
scope of this PR, and the whole family ships for sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [691b6bb](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/691b6bb96ecaffc72689eceb41fa244b33f7b1d4)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T12:52:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc_head_det_train): per-H 64-bit SM100/103 kernels, SM107 L2 bulk-reduce acc bwd (#9162)

The mHC head is the final unweighted mean over 4 streams, in BF16. It
has three timed ops: forward (`fwd`) `Y = X.mean(dim=1)`, backward
(`bwd`) `dX = BF16(dY/4)` and accumulating backward (`acc`) `dX +=
BF16(dY/4)`. Hidden sizes are 4096, 5120 and 7168 on SM100/SM103 and
4096 on SM107. The head ships in two packages: a deterministic package,
`cake_mhc_head_det_train` (`det`), and a non-deterministic-named twin,
`cake_mhc_head_nondet_train` (`nondet`), that runs the same kernels.
This PR updates both.

All times are CUPTI GPU time with a cold L2 before every call. The A/B
arms (main, this PR, and a main-vs-main A/A arm that gives the A/A band)
were interleaved on the same GPU, rotating through all six arm orders,
over 12 rounds (8 on R200) x 100 calls. The non-Cake arms were
torch.compile (default and max-autotune-no-cudagraphs) and an autotuned
hand-written Triton kernel on PyTorch 2.14.1 / Triton 3.8.0, timed
against this PR in a separate same-process run of 10 rounds. The kernels
were built with CUDA 13.4. GPUs: B200 (sm_100a), GB200 (sm_100a), GB300
(sm_103a), R200 (sm_107a). Speedup = baseline µs / this PR µs (> 1 =
this PR is faster).

### [8323e49](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8323e49c7ccd176cc204eab82ce6fcecd2de3a2b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T12:51:38Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_train): backward wait hint on SM100 / SM103 and a per-architecture NoPE dKV window (#9163)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_train` contains the
non-deterministic Cake training kernels for DeepSeek Sparse Attention.
They implement top-k sparse MLA with absorbed queries and use 64 query
heads and BF16 inputs and outputs (plus an optional FP32 trainer dKV
accumulator). They accumulate dK / dV in FP32 with unordered atomics.
The kernels come in two forms, RoPE (query / key 576 = 512 latent + 64
rope, value 512) and NoPE (query / key / value 512), and each form has a
forward and a backward. 14 kernel programs per architecture cover the
packed-576 and pre-256 query layouts, trainer dKV accumulation and the
dKV destination row map. This PR changes only the backward on SM100 /
SM103. The RoPE and NoPE backward kernels now pass a 10 ms suspend-time
hint to their mbarrier waits. The NoPE backward now keeps its persistent
token loop up to a 128 MiB FP32 dKV window (was 64 MiB). The forward
kernels are unchanged, and SM107 keeps the hint-free wait and the 64 MiB
window. The baseline is the previous Cake version (FlashInfer main; this
package is unchanged from fdd17bae, the measured tree, to 0897cd597,
this PR's base). Against it, backward / step speedups on the customer
issue shapes (T 16384, S 65536, top-k 2048) are:
- GB300: NoPE 1.029x / 1.021x, RoPE 1.011x / 1.009x
- B200: NoPE 1.014x / 1.011x, RoPE 1.013x / 1.018x

Other rows are within noise of main or faster, except three GB300 rows
that are 0.2-0.4 % slower (doc_4096 step 0.998x, doc_16384 backward
0.996x and step 0.997x; the doc_4096 ckpt row built from that step is
0.998x) and the B200 doc_4096 backward (0.990x in the first run; 0.995x
on two GPUs in a repeat run, table below). Main has no deterministic
Cake version of this kernel, so the comparison with
`flashinfer.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_det_train` (draft PR #9161) is
pending. Against the fastest same-precision non-Cake implementation (all
rows without †), Cake is faster on every row except:
- nope_short_1024_k128 forward vs FlashMLA: GB300 0.793x, B200 0.785x
- nope_short_1024_k128 backward / step vs FA4 sparse-MLA: GB300 0.925x /
0.892x, B200 0.487x / 0.485x, R200 0.875x / 0.793x. The ckpt rows built
from them are slower as well.
- Parity:
  - RoPE customer-shape forward vs FA4: GB300 0.997x, B200 0.996x
  - R200 nope_tail_2048x65536 forward vs FA4 sparse-MLA: 0.993x
- R200 nope_short_1024_k128 forward vs FA4 sparse-MLA: 1.018x paired,
0.993x from the ms columns

These gaps predate this PR: the forward is unchanged, and the short NoPE
backward stays within noise of main. The FA4 sparse-MLA arm calls FA4's
private forward / backward without autograd. Cake's time includes its
public autograd entry, which dominates this small row. For reference
only, ratios against BF16 dK / dV implementations:
- RoPE: B200 repro8949_rope backward / step 0.976x / 0.990x; R200 cuDNN
backward / step on doc_4096 0.931x / 0.971x and doc_16384 0.918x /
0.960x, and repro8949_rope backward 0.984x.
- NoPE (not shown in the tables): B200 repro8949_nope backward cuDNN
0.996x, nope_short_1024_k128 backward cuDNN 0.619x and step FlashMLA +
cuDNN 0.651x; R200 repro8949_nope backward cuDNN 0.970x.

- Software: CUDA 13.4 (kernels JIT-compiled with nvcc 13.4.2), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, cuDNN 9.24.0, cuDNN frontend 1.32.2.
- Timing:
- Each call is timed as a CUPTI span, from first to last GPU activity.
L2 is flushed before each call (cold L2), in eager mode, after a 5 s
burn-in.
- Per process, the time is the median over 10 rounds of the per-round
median call.
- main ms / PR ms: median over processes. main and PR are interleaved
base / PR / PR / base on one GPU, with 2-3 main and 2-5 PR processes per
row; the PR count includes the baseline processes.
- A/A band: the larger max/min spread of the main processes and of the
PR processes. It is a lower bound on run-to-run noise. On R200, where
main and PR run the same code, 8 of the 33 fwd / bwd / step rows differ
beyond it (largest: repro8949_nope forward 0.987x, band ±1.09 %).
- vs non-Cake: the median of non-Cake time / Cake time within each
baseline process (> 1 = Cake faster).
- The baseline process can run on a different GPU of the node than the
main / PR columns, so its ms / PR ms can differ slightly from the ratio.
- cuDNN has 2-3 processes per row; FA4, FA4 sparse-MLA and FlashMLA +
cuDNN have one.
  - Ratios within about 1 % of 1.0 are parity.
- step = forward + backward. ckpt is the checkpointed training step (2 x
forward + backward), computed as the fwd + step medians. Its non-Cake
column sums the same baseline's fwd and step times, so the ratio is not
paired. Its band is the larger of the fwd and step bands.
- Comparison rule: forward rows compare with the fastest of all
baselines. Backward, step and ckpt rows compare with the fastest
FP32-dKV baseline. No FP32-dKV non-Cake RoPE backward was measured (the
FA4 sparse-MLA arm covers NoPE only), so † rows show the fastest
BF16-dKV implementation for reference.
- Baselines:
- cuDNN: cuDNN frontend DSA sparse attention plans (its backward returns
dK / dV in BF16).
- FA4: flash-attn-4 4.0.0b38 public sparse attention (BF16 dK / dV
output).
- FA4 sparse-MLA: the flash-attn-4 4.0.0b38 forward plus its sparse-MLA
backward. This backward returns dV in an FP32 buffer, which makes it the
only non-Cake backward with an FP32 dKV output. It was measured for NoPE
only.
- FlashMLA + cuDNN: FlashMLA sparse forward (commit ba89a346 for RoPE
d_qk 576, main 395cb3af for NoPE d_qk 512) plus the cuDNN backward.

This is the only Cake DSA sparse-attention training package: it is
non-deterministic, and a deterministic package (#9161) is in review and
not on main. The related Cake DSA indexer ships as separate
deterministic and non-deterministic training packages, and this family
ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

---------

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [799c47e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/799c47e776b43c76fbc7d572afc358b4b197f609)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T12:29:32Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d_det_kcp): packed FP32 backward, one-SM-short forward (#9142)

The Cake packed width-4 depthwise causal conv1d + SiLU training kernel
(BF16 activations, FP32 accumulation) has four forms: deterministic and
non-deterministic, each single-rank and context-parallel (KCP). The
single-rank forms also take BF16 taps and an optional bias. The KCP
forms take FP32 taps and no bias. This PR updates the deterministic KCP
form (`flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_det_train_kcp`:
`cake_causal_conv1d_det_kcp` / `cake_causal_conv1d_det_kcp_multi`). It
changes the default backward route (`cooperative=False`) and the
forward. The baseline is the previous Cake version: the same package on
FlashInfer main, as shipped by #9111, run back to back on the same GPU.

Default route (`cooperative=False`), B200 / GB300 / VR200:
- bwd: 1.099x-1.145x / 1.024x-1.094x / 1.082x-1.115x
- fwd+bwd: 1.053x-1.078x / 1.012x-1.054x / 1.039x-1.070x
- checkpointed step: 1.036x-1.053x / 1.009x-1.038x / 1.032x-1.053x
- fwd beside a 2 ms side kernel: 1.223x-1.332x / 1.295x-1.394x /
1.160x-1.300x
- fwd alone: 0.989x-1.000x / 0.980x-0.999x / 0.993x-1.013x; slower
beyond the A/A band: B200 8 of 9 shapes, up to 1.1% (3.5 us); GB300 7 of
9, up to 2.0% (4.4 us); VR200 5 of 9, up to 0.7% (1.2 us)

`cooperative=True` (its backward launch is the same as on main; its
fwd+bwd and checkpointed-step rows include the changed forward), B200 /
GB300 / VR200:
- bwd: 0.998x-1.003x / 0.999x-1.004x / 0.997x-1.021x; slower: B200 1 of
9, 0.2% (1.0 us); GB300 1 of 9, 0.1% (0.5 us); VR200 2 of 9, up to 0.3%
(1.5 us)
- fwd+bwd: 0.996x-1.000x / 0.993x-1.000x / 0.981x-1.007x; slower: B200 9
of 9, up to 0.4% (3.6 us); GB300 6 of 9, up to 0.7% (4.7 us); VR200 2 of
9, up to 2.0% (8.7 us)
- checkpointed step: 0.995x-0.996x / 0.992x-0.999x / 0.986x-1.008x;
slower: B200 9 of 9, up to 0.5% (7.2 us); GB300 8 of 9, up to 0.8% (8.9
us); VR200 3 of 9, up to 1.4% (8.8 us)

*Table 1. Default route (`cooperative=False`), 9 shapes per GPU on B200,
GB300 and VR200. Times are in microseconds, each the slowest rank. They
are measured with CUDA events around the phase, cold L2, and host
enqueue hidden behind a short spin on the stream ("ahead" timing). Each
run is the median of 12 interleaved rounds. Runs go main, this PR, this
PR, main on the same GPU(s). Main is the mean of runs 1 and 4; this PR
is the mean of runs 2 and 3. Speedup = main / this PR (above 1: this PR
faster). A/A band = max(|run1 - run4| / main, |run2 - run3| / this PR).
A row counts as faster or slower only when its speedup differs from 1 by
more than the band. Slower-than-band counts and sizes in the summary use
the unrounded measurements, so a row printed as 1.000x can count as
slower. In "up to X% (Y us)", the largest relative and the largest
absolute slowdown can come from different shapes. "fwd, 2 ms side
kernel": a one-thread 2 ms spin kernel is already resident on another
stream when the forward is enqueued. The time is the median, over the
same 12 rounds, of that loaded span (the slowest rank in each round).
Checkpointed step = 2 fwd + bwd. CPn = context parallel over n ranks.
PyTorch 2.14.1 (CUDA 13.0 runtime); kernels built with CUDA 13.4.2.
B200: sm_100a, 148 SMs. GB300: sm_103a, 152 SMs. VR200: sm_107a, 212
SMs.*

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* The causal convolution forward pass uses a grid one SM smaller when it
can cover all channel tiles, and the full grid when needed. It reports
an error if the full grid cannot cover them.
  * Forward results remain independent of the launch grid.
* **Documentation**
  * Clarified forward grid selection and co-resident execution behavior.
* **Tests**
* Added coverage for grid selection, insufficient capacity, and bitwise
equivalence with the unpartitioned forward pass.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [8067a45](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8067a45ad10308e0377d694f02e1661975147f28)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T12:22:54Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc_det): SM103 fwd keeps L2-hinted X read to 6656 (was 6144) (#9157)

- **Change:** This PR changes one routing rule in the Cake four-stream
mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connection) training kernel (BF16
residual streams X [T, 4, H], FP32 mixing parameters; H 4096 / 5120 /
7168 on SM100 and SM103, 4096 on SM107). On SM103 (GB300) at H 4096
only, for T 6145 to 6656, the forward mapping pass now loads X with L2
priority EVICT_NORMAL instead of EVICT_FIRST; EVICT_NORMAL previously
stopped at T 6144. The same one-line change is made in
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train` and `flashinfer.cake_mhc_nondet_train`;
the kernels are unchanged and only the cache-policy operand of the X
loads differs at those token counts, so the deterministic package's
outputs are bitwise identical to main.
- **Deterministic result:** The baseline is the same package on current
main (the previous Cake version), timed on the same GPU in the same
process. On GB300, the 9 rows whose route changes (H 4096, T 6145 / 6400
/ 6656) are 1.013x to 1.026x faster than main: forward is 1.013-1.024x,
forward with L2 flushed between its two passes is 1.016-1.026x, and
checkpointed backward (forward recompute + backward) is 1.014-1.018x.
The noise band on those rows is about [0.99, 1.007]. Every other row on
GB300, B200 (sm_100a) and R200 (sm_107a) runs identical kernels on both
sides and is within noise, so no row is slower than main beyond noise.
- **Non-deterministic:** On GB300, the 9 rows whose route changes are
1.010x to 1.028x faster than main (noise band [0.987, 1.005]), and every
other row runs identical kernels and is within noise. On B200 and R200,
its kernels and routes are unchanged.

Time is GPU kernel time per call in microseconds (sum of kernel active
time measured with CUPTI), with L2 flushed before every timed call. Each
session interleaves main, this PR and a second copy of main, and after 8
warm-up calls it runs 6 groups of 32 calls and takes the median of the
per-group medians; the tables show the median over valid sessions, where
a session is valid when main is within 1 % of its second copy. Speedup
is main / PR (above 1 means this PR is faster), and the noise band is
the range of main / PR over all rows whose kernels are identical on both
sides (an A/A measurement), widened for a changed-route row to include
that row's own main-against-main range.

Cake also ships this kernel in a non-deterministic mode
(`flashinfer.cake_mhc_nondet_train`, which mirrors this rule) and as a

and the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [5c29500](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5c29500371e87cf53610b09970447a01cd65c1a1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T12:21:48Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_moe_grouped_gemm_det_train): fused FP32 wgrad accumulate, up to 1.25x faster (#9132)

`flashinfer.cake_moe_grouped_gemm_det_train` is Cake's deterministic
(bitwise run-to-run) ragged BF16 MoE grouped GEMM for training, one of
two variants Cake ships for this kernel. This PR updates the
deterministic variant in three ways. It adds a fused FP32
weight-gradient accumulate into the caller's `main_grad` that gives the
same bits as `out.add_(dW)`. It adds L2 evict-first forms of the wide
forward and data-gradient programs. It also takes the 512-wide
weight-gradient k tile from 3072 rows per group (was 4096) on
sm_100a/sm_103a. Against FlashInfer main's deterministic package, across
all 210 shapes per GPU, no shape is slower beyond the A/A noise band,
and 45 GB300 shapes and 37 B200 shapes are faster beyond it. The peak
speedups are 1.254x (GB300) and 1.215x (B200), both on `wgrad_acc32 dn
E32 131072 bal`. The tables also compare each shape against the fastest
non-Cake implementation of the same op at the same precision (BF16
inputs, FP32 accumulation).

<details>
<summary>NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a): pass 1, all 210 shapes</summary>

R200 (sm_107a) and GB200 rows are pending while measurement is in
progress.

- **Shape**: op, projection, experts `E`, total rows, group-size
distribution, output.
- **Projection**: `gu` = gate/up (N 4096, K 6144); `dn` = down (N 6144,
K 2048); `gu+dn` = both in one block.
- **Distribution and output**: `bal` = equal groups; `skew` = 4:3:2:1
groups; `1-empty` = one empty group; `short16` = 16 groups of 64-484
rows beside 16 groups of 7918 rows; `f32` = FP32 dW output (BF16
otherwise).
- **Ops**: `fwd`, `dgrad` and `wgrad`; `wgrad_acc32` = weight gradient
accumulated into an FP32 `main_grad`; `wgrad_acc16` = the same into a
BF16 `main_grad` (no non-Cake implementation exists at this precision,
so the column shows `none`); `bwd` = dgrad + wgrad; `bwd_acc32` /
`step_acc32` = with FP32 `main_grad` accumulate; `step` = checkpointed 2
x forward + backward; `block` = checkpointed gate/up -> SwiGLU -> down;
`_es` = the same with PyTorch early stop on.
- **Non-Cake**: `quack` = QuACK 0.6.5 varlen grouped GEMM; `cute_moe` =
CUTLASS 4.8.1 CuTe DSL MoE grouped GEMM; `cublaslt_grp` = cuBLASLt 13.10
grouped matmul; `cudnnfe` = cuDNN frontend BF16 grouped GEMM; `te_gg` /
`te_gl_grouped` / `te_gl_grouped_sw` = Transformer Engine 2.20.2 grouped
GEMM / GroupedLinear; `torch_gmm_ag` = `torch._grouped_mm` (PyTorch
2.14.1); `cbl_acc` = per-expert cuBLAS accumulating into FP32;
`fimm_cublaslt` = per-expert cuBLASLt; `fi_cudnn_tac` = cuDNN graph
grouped matmul.

Cake's other variant, `flashinfer.cake_moe_grouped_gemm_nondet_train`,
has the same entry points, and both variants ship on sm_100a, sm_103a
and sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Eligible fp32 weight-gradient accumulations can now add directly to
the output, avoiding scratch-buffer allocation; other cases continue to
use a scratch-based route. Both routes produce identical results.
* Expanded grouped-GEMM kernel support across additional GPU
architectures and configurations, with updated launch planning for long
reductions.

* **Tests**
* Expanded coverage for reproducibility, accumulation, GPU
architecture-specific planning, graph replay, and training scenarios.

* **Documentation**
* Updated guidance on accumulation routes, reproducibility, supported
builds, and scratch-memory costs.

### [45c822b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/45c822b858a6a7c38e0ea7437868d04ed4e2e54c)

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_det_train): faster backward routes for residual H 6144, H 2048, H 4096 and FP32-weight H 5120 on SM100, SM103 and SM107 (#9134)

The Cake deterministic RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_det_train`) has variants by input form (2-D
rows, strided rows, per-head 3-D q/k inputs), weight precision (BF16
activations with a BF16 or an FP32 weight) and fused form (plain, or
residual-add fused), each with a forward and a backward. This PR
delivers faster backward routes on all three architectures. On sm_100a,
plain H 2048 (BF16 weight) gets faster at T = 4096 and T = 65536, plain
H 4096 (BF16 weight) at T = 14928 to 32768, residual-fused H 6144 (BF16
weight) at T = 64 to 65536 and H 5120 (FP32 weight) at T = 65536. On
sm_103a, plain H 2048 gets faster at T = 4096, plain H 4096 at T = 14928
to 32768 and residual-fused H 6144 at T = 64 to 65536. On sm_107a,
residual-fused H 6144 gets faster at T = 1024 to 65536. The baseline is
the current version of the same Cake kernel on FlashInfer main.

Changed routes cover 87 cells on sm_100a, 87 on sm_103a and 36 on
sm_107a. Per architecture, the 572 timed cells (143 rows x 4 ops) are 75
faster / 497 neutral / 0 slower on sm_100a, 69 / 502 / 1 on sm_103a and
24 / 548 / 0 on sm_107a. Every faster cell is on a changed route, and no
changed-route cell is slower on any architecture. The one slower cell is
a same-route cell on sm_103a, where both packages launch the same
program with identical machine code: residual-fused H 6144 BF16, T = 64,
forward, 3.07 us on main vs 3.14 us on the PR (0.980, A/A band ±1.6%).
An 8-process re-measure of that cell gives 3.200 us on main vs 3.168 us
on the PR (1.010, A/A band ±2.0%), with per-process ratios on both sides
of 1, so the cell is neutral. The largest backward gains are residual H
6144 at T = 64 on sm_100a (1.373) and sm_103a (1.298), and at T = 4096
on sm_107a (1.293).

13.4.92 | 75 / 497 / 0 | 75 / 12 / 0 | 0 / 485 / 0 | 0.84% / 9.65% |

13.4.92 | 69 / 502 / 1 | 69 / 18 / 0 | 0 / 484 / 1 | 0.79% / 12.50% |
| sm_107a | NVIDIA Graphics Device | 212 | 620.43 | 2.14.1+cu130 (13.0)
| 13.4.92 | 24 / 548 / 0 | 24 / 12 / 0 | 0 / 536 / 0 | 0.99% / 9.09% |

The sm_107a GPU is a VR200. Its driver reports the name "NVIDIA Graphics
Device".

Each latency is the median CUPTI span of one CUDA-graph replay, with L2
flushed before every replay. The persisting-L2 lines are reset before
each flush, so lines kept by an L2 evict-last hint cannot stay resident.
Each row was timed in 4 separate processes with alternating arm order (2
forward, 2 reverse) and 200 replays per arm and operation in each. A
byte-identical copy of each package was loaded a second time from
another path to measure the A/A noise band. The band is calibrated on
same-route cells (cells where both packages launch the same programs).
Speedup = main / PR. A cell is faster (or slower) only when all 4
per-session ratios agree and the pooled ratio is beyond 1 ± the A/A
band. Otherwise it is neutral.

Shape labels: H is the hidden size and T the token (row) count. `bf16`
means BF16 activations with a BF16 weight, `f32` means an FP32 weight
with BF16 activations, `res` is the residual-add fused form, `(row
stride 576)` is a strided-row input, and `k[T,4,256]` / `q[T,24,256]
strided` are per-head 3-D inputs. Ops: `bwd` is backward, `fwdbwd` is
forward+backward and `step` is a training step.

### [0f99bf7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0f99bf70c3bfe0fe2de210d14c120073633513cf)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T12:17:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): sm_100a one-stage FP8 context form programs (#9160)

Cake's FP8 paged-context attention (FP8 Q/K/V, head dim 128) ships AOT
runtime-size programs at GQA packs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 16. It
has six forms. One is plain causal. The other five are flag forms: NC
(non-causal), LSE (causal with LSE output), SINK (causal with sinks),
NC_LSE and NC_SINK.

Today on sm_100a (B200), the five flag forms run the two-stage form
programs `RUNTIME_PACK<p>_<FORM>`. Each tile has two 128-row query
stages. When a call's query tile fits in one stage, the second stage is
empty.

A previous PR added 20 one-Q-stage programs,
`RUNTIME_PACK<p>_<FORM>_PX_Q1`, for the five flag forms at packs 1, 2, 4
and 8. That PR built them for sm_103a (GB300) only. These programs use a
4-stage K/V ring, a swapped P tile (P stored in the other stage's S
columns) and one Q stage. This PR builds the same 20 `_PX_Q1` programs
for sm_100a. It routes sm_100a flag-form calls at packs 1, 2, 4 and 8 to
them when the query tile fits one stage, at every key count. A tile fits
one stage when it has at most 128 query rows after GQA packing, which
means at most 128 / pack query tokens. Other sm_100a calls are
unchanged. sm_103a routes are unchanged. The arithmetic does not change.
O and LSE are bitwise equal to the previous program and to the JIT
module in every timed row and layout.

The 65 routed rows are 1.044x to 1.500x faster than the previous Cake
program. The 45 rows with more than 128 keys are 1.329x to 1.500x
faster. The 20 rows with 64 or 128 keys are 1.044x to 1.144x faster.
Every routed row is faster than the previous program and the JIT module
in each of the 10 memory layouts. No row is slower. Compared with
trtllm-gen, the routed rows are 1.061x to 4.812x faster.

**B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4. GPU time with cold L2 (CUPTI),
median over 10 seeded memory layouts x 2 rounds.**

- Shape is batch x query tokens x key/value tokens per request.
- q/kv heads are the query and KV head counts.
- Page is the KV page size in tokens.
- "Previous Cake" is the program that FlashInfer main routes the call to
before this PR: the two-stage `RUNTIME_PACK<p>_<FORM>` program.
- trtllm-gen is a second baseline.
- Ratios are medians of the per-layout ratios. A value above 1 means
this PR is faster.
- Rows marked "(unchanged)" have 132 query rows per tile and keep the
previous program. Their ratio is 1.000 to 1.0004.

The family also ships the plain causal FP8 form and BF16 paged-context
programs on both sm_100a and sm_103a, and with this PR the flag-form
one-stage programs ship on both sm_100a and sm_103a.

### [1929d57](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1929d5795016590216cd079b5beb93b1a92d6977)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T12:06:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): sm_107a l6 and CTA-pair l6 draw their work units from tickets (#9153)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train` scores the deterministic DSA
indexer and computes the exact top-k for training. It has two variants:
BF16 scores (BF16 q/k) and FP8 scores (e4m3 q/k with a per-key FP32
scale). This PR changes only the BF16 variant on sm_107a. Before, its
six l6 and CTA-pair l6 scan programs used a fixed list of work units for
each CTA. Now they take work units from a ticket counter. The ticket
counter is a global atomic counter that gives the next unit to the next
free CTA. The sm_100a and sm_103a programs already work this way. As a
result, when another stream holds even one SM, a call no longer waits
for a full second wave of CTAs (#7548). On each of the three GPUs, ids,
scores and order stay bitwise identical to main on all 66 rows. On
sm_100a and sm_103a, this PR changes no dispatch. The kernel sources
there differ from main only in the integer literal suffixes that a newer
code generator writes (for example, `16` becomes `16ll`).

- R200, real context-parallel rank inputs: doc262k_topic ranks are up to
1.137x faster (r00). packed11_topic ranks r00 to r09 are 1.019x to
1.104x faster. The pack4k-64k ranks are 1.062x and 1.086x faster. In
total, 30 of 66 rows are faster beyond noise.
- R200, second stream (#7548): on main, one resident block on another
stream makes these calls 1.42x to 1.91x slower than free running. With
this PR, the held/free ratio is 0.94x to 1.05x. The held speedup over
main is 1.402x to 1.775x with one resident block and 1.352x to 1.602x
with 32 full SMs.
- R200, 12 rows slower than main beyond noise. This is the accepted cost
of the ticket counter on balanced shapes:
- V5 0.965x, S3 0.969x, S2 0.973x, glm2k_16k 0.973x, s3_cold16k 0.973x,
Z2cp 0.973x, s2_4x2k_packed 0.974x, C3 0.977x, packed11_topic_r15
0.984x, P3 0.986x, packed11_topic_r13 0.986x, P1 0.987x.
- V5, Z2cp, packed11_topic_r15 and packed11_topic_r13 were rerun in 4
rounds. Their PR/main time is 1.030 to 1.037 for V5 (mean 1.032), 1.028
to 1.034 for Z2cp (mean 1.031), 1.017 to 1.021 for packed11_topic_r15
and 1.014 to 1.015 for packed11_topic_r13.
- B200 and GB300: no row is slower than main beyond noise (66 rows
each).

Both versions run in the same process with CUPTI kernel timing, cold L2
and three arm orders (AB, BA, interleaved). Speedup is main latency / PR
latency, so a value above 1 means the PR is faster. The A/A band comes
from timing the same package twice. A row is slower beyond noise if its
speedup is below 1 - max(A/A band, 1%).

The residency rows measure one call while a kernel on another stream
holds SMs. Each value is the median of 7 calls per configuration, timed
with CUDA events, with interleaved arms. "1 resident block" is the #7548
repro: a side stream runs `torch.cuda._sleep`, which keeps one block
resident. "32 full SMs" runs 32 CTAs. Each CTA uses the largest opt-in
shared memory, so one CTA fills one SM. speedup (held) is main held ms /
PR held ms.

### [48d16dc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/48d16dcd8c3eb514ee5092b705ed60be1f8533b9)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-08T11:59:41Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dsv4): bound source-exact decode rows by num_query_tokens (#9156)

`cake_dsv4` (DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA decode/prefill) ships 57 programs
covering 37 distinct variants. The variants cover BF16 and FP8 KV caches
with H8/H16, H32, H64 and H128 heads. This PR re-exports the five
source-exact decode programs: `bf16_h8_h16_source_exact` and
`fp8_h8_h16_source_exact` on sm_100a and sm_103a, and
`fp8_h64_source_exact`, which is one program shared by both
architectures. After this change, every row is bounded by the metadata
row count T (`num_query_tokens`). On a padded ragged call (T <
`cum_seq_lens_q[B]`), a call form that used to read and write past row
T, rows at or past T are now neither read nor written. Outputs of valid
calls (non-decreasing `cum_seq_lens_q` starting at 0) are bitwise
unchanged. The baseline is the previous Cake version (FlashInfer main).

Latency is in us: the median over 6 rounds of CUDA graph replay with a
warm L2. Speedup = main / PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster.
